title: QBR framework & tech-ask tracker — Dedicated/Private upsell playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a lightweight, customer-facing QBR outline combined with an internal tracker for technical asks that lead to Dedicated/Private upgrades or premium SLA add-ons. Use this to run discovery during QBRs, prioritize technical blockers, and convert operational pain into concrete expansion motions.

Intended audience:
- Customer Success Managers (primary)
- Solutions Engineers (technical validation)
- Account Execs (commercial negotiation)
- SRE/Platform partner (feasibility and sizing)

High-level play: 
1) During QBR, surface 3 measurable pain points tied to unit economics or reliability (latency tail, token cost, outage incidents).
2) Map each pain to a concrete uplift (Dedicated capacity / Private deployment / SLA uplift).
3) Use the Tech-Ask Tracker below to collect scope, constraints, and decision owner.
4) Run a 10-day rapid feasibility thread (design + rough cost estimate + migration window).
5) Offer a 90-day pilot or commitment corridor for Dedicated or Private with SLA trial.

QBR Agenda (30–45 min, customer-facing template):
- 0–5m: Welcome, attendees, recap of last quarter agreements and action items
- 5–12m: Usage highlights (tokens, peak RPS, top routes), cost KPIs, and any incidents since last QBR
- 12–20m: Health & quality (latency percentile trends, error rates, model regressions, eval snapshots)
- 20–30m: Opportunity map — 3 prioritized improvement areas (mapped to product levers: batching, caching, model variant, dedicated)
content_continued:
- 30–38m: Technical ask deep-dive (owner, blocker, business impact, desired timeline)
- 38–45m: Commercial options and next steps (pilot proposal, PO timelines, stakeholder approvals)

(Insert appendix: one-slide PDF of dedicated vs private comparison; link later)

Tech-Ask Tracker (quick table; rows are examples you can copy into a sheet):
- Customer: Acme Analytics | Ask ID: TA-001 | Short ask: Reduce 99.9p latency spikes during batched scoring | Impact: 20% reduction in tail latency -> 18% lower P99 SLA breaches -> $15k/mo savings | Proposed uplift: Move hot routes to Dedicated with 2x capacity isolation | Owner (customer): Daniel K. (Infra) | Redwood owner: Arjun P. | Dependencies: model shard config, autoscale policy | Est. effort: 3 engineer-days + 2 SRE-days | Decision timeframe: 6 weeks | Status: discovery
- Customer: Nova Retail | Ask ID: TA-002 | Short ask: Data residency + certified KMS for PII prompts | Impact: Required for SOC2 + EU-reg compliance -> enables enterprise contract | Proposed uplift: Private deployment (VPC) + KMS integration | Owner: Sophia L. (Security) | Redwood owner: Sofia M. | Dependencies: network peering, audit logs export | Est. effort: 4 weeks | Decision timeframe: Q1 renewal | Status: proposal

Risk & Priority rubric (use to score tech-asks):
- Business impact: 0 (cosmetic) -> 5 (revenue blocker)
- Urgency: 0 ("nice-to-have") -> 5 (compliance / legal deadline)
- Implementation complexity: 0 (config) -> 5 (architecture + infra change)
- Convertibility to revenue: 0 (low) -> 5 (direct expansion/capex)
Score = (Business impact * 3) + (Urgency * 2) - Complexity. Prioritize highest score for pilot offers.

Dedicated upgrade sizing primer (for SE + SRE):
- Inputs required from customer: peak concurrent requests, average tokens per request, target P50/P95/P99 latency, preferred model family and quantization profile.
- Quick estimate formula (rule-of-thumb): GPU_count = ceil((peak_tokens_per_sec * avg_compute_per_token) / gpu_tokens_per_sec_capacity)
- Example: peak 10k tokens/sec; avg_compute_per_token 0.00008 GPU-seconds; GPU capacity 40k tokens/sec => GPU_count = ceil((10k * 0.00008) / (40k * 0.000001)) => simplified to an initial 1–2 GPU recommendation; always validate with perf benching.
- Sizing note: leave 30–40% headroom for burst/rolling deploys. If customer's SLA requires sub-200ms P95, recommend Dedicated with hot-route isolation and autoscale policy tuned to burst window.

Private deployment checklist (migration readiness):
- Legal/Procurement: signed MSA addendum for Private hosting (Legal)
- Networking: support for IP ranges, peering/Transit gateway, and VPN or Direct Connect
- Security: customer KMS details, IP allowlist, audit log sink (SIEM integration)
- Data flow: confirmation of what data is sent to Redwood control plane vs kept local
- Ops: runbook for support handoff, escalation matrix, and monthly operational sync cadence
- Cutover window: recommended 48–72h warm-up + canary 10% traffic for 72h

SLA uplift play (pricing & negotiation levers):
- Base hosted plan -> premium SLA tiers (Bronze/Silver/Gold):
  - Bronze: 99.5% uptime, 200ms P95 (extra fee: ~+15% usage)
  - Silver: 99.9% uptime, 150ms P95, faster incident response SLA (extra fee: ~+35%)
  - Gold: 99.95% uptime, 100ms P95, dedicated on-call routing, custom runbooks (price: bespoke, often tied to committed monthly reserved spend)
- Commercial levers: commitment length, upfront reservation (dedicated pool), data-retention & audit package, embedding volume discounts.
- Concessions to use sparingly: free pilot CPU/GPU credits, extended support hours for 90 days, reduced penalty for early termination only when linked to signed Dedicated commitment.

Customer communication artifacts (templates to copy & personalize):
- QBR summary email: subject: "QBR recap + prioritized tech asks & next steps" — include 3 bullets (what changed, ask IDs, proposed commercial option) and call to action for a decision owner and date.
- Pilot kickoff note: include monitoring SLOs, canary percentage, rollback criteria, and escalation contacts.

Internal RACI (simplified):
- CSM: discovery, commercial narrative, QBR management (Responsible)
- SE: technical validation, SOW-level scoping, benching (Accountable)
- SRE/Platform: sizing review, runbook inputs, migration window (Consulted)
- Legal/RevOps: contract changes and billing cadence (Informed / Accountable for contracting)

Conversion play ideas (experiments to A/B in the wild):
- "Low-friction canary" — 30-day low-cost Dedicated pilot for top-3 hot routes; charge minimal onboarding and require 3-month commit if SLOs met.
- "Compliance fast-path" — fixed scoping + turnkey Private deployment for EU customers with templated network setup to reduce procurement cycle by 40%.
- "SLA swap" — trade incremental committed spend for faster incident response and guaranteed MTTRemedy windows.

Open questions / TODOs (for this doc):
- Build a minimal sheet view that auto-calculates risk score and suggests initial commercial tier (Bronze/Silver/Gold) — owner: Arjun.
- Create one-slide comparison of Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted+SLA for customer-facing QBR appendix — owner: Sofia.
- Draft pilot pricing templates (engineering cost + margin) for 30/90/180-day pilots — owner: Evan.

Quick wins to include in QBR before asking for commitment:
- Implement route-level caching for top-5 heavy embedding endpoints (likely 10–20% cost reduction)
- Toggle model variants for non-sensitive traffic to reduce GPU cost; quantify savings and present as committed-offset in the proposal

Appendix: sample short email (copyable)
Subject: QBR recap & next step — Dedicated pilot for hot-route stability
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the productive QBR earlier. We captured 3 technical asks and recommend a 60-day Dedicated pilot scoped to the top two hot routes (TA-001, TA-004). Proposed next step: 30-minute tech alignment call this week to lock scope and an internal SOW.
Best,
<Maya>

----
Notes on doc posture: This file is intentionally a hybrid: part QBR-slate that you can paste into a customer slide deck; part internal tracker for prioritizing and sizing technical asks. Keep iterations frequent — the value is in moving fast from discovery to a small pilot with measurable SLOs.
